answer: An AI agent economy can achieve robust Sybil resistance by requiring cryptographic proofs of compute-bound workloads, forcing an attacker to wander through vast search spaces just to generate a single valid identity token. This prevents adversaries from scaling malicious nodes cheaply. If a rogue cluster attempts to flood the network, the computational expense triggers an immediate economic ripple, driving up hardware and energy costs per node equivalent to the physical mass of a walnut of silicon processing power.
